architect.prompt:
Directive: Apply the Builder pattern to refactor table construction and configuration logic

Goal
- Reorganize construction and configuration code for Table/HTable into a fluent Builder API so construction logic is centralized, explicit, and easier to extend and test — without changing external behavior (refactor, not new functionality).
- Maintain backwards compatibility during the transition by keeping existing constructors/setters deprecated but functional, delegating to the builder.
- Ensure configuration defaults are sourced from ConnectionConfiguration (expose rpcTimeout) and ConnectionImplementation supplies a pre-configured builder.

Scope / Target classes
- TableBuilderBase (new abstract base for builders)
- TableBuilder (concrete builder for building Table/HTable instances)
- ConnectionImplementation (or the concrete Connection class)
- ConnectionConfiguration (extend to expose rpcTimeout)
- HTable (concrete Table implementation)
- Table (public interface / factory API)
- Any factory helper methods (getTable, getTableBuilder)

Architectural intent & responsibilities
- TableBuilderBase: hold common builder state, provide fluent setters for all configuration options currently available on HTable (timeouts, scanners, RPC settings, metrics toggles, etc.). Provide validation and defaulting logic common to all table builders. Make this class the single place to evolve construction options.
- TableBuilder: concrete builder that knows how to construct the concrete Table implementation(s) (HTable). It should accept a Connection or ConnectionImplementation and TableName (or similar) as inputs and produce a fully configured HTable on build().
- ConnectionImplementation: provide a method getTableBuilder(TableName) that returns a TableBuilder pre-populated with configuration derived from this connection (including ConnectionConfiguration values). Deprecate direct getTable variants that bypass the builder; have getTable delegate to getTableBuilder().build() so behavior is unchanged.
- ConnectionConfiguration: add an accessor for rpcTimeout and any other configuration parameters the builder needs. Keep ConnectionConfiguration the source of truth for default values.
- HTable: become effectively immutable after construction. Remove direct configuration logic from HTable (constructors should be minimal, accepting a TableBuilder or the resolved set of configuration parameters). Keep the previous setters and constructors but mark them @Deprecated and implement them as thin wrappers that forward to or mutate builder-state-compatible fields so existing code continues to work.
- Table (API): augment with getTableBuilder/getTable(...) delegation so callers can choose the fluent builder or the old style (which still delegates to the builder).

Design details and constraints
- Fluent API: builder methods return this (TableBuilder) to allow chaining: builder.rpcTimeout(...).readRpcTimeout(...).maxAttempts(...).build().
- Single source of defaults: builder should obtain defaults from ConnectionConfiguration at creation. Individual builder setters override those defaults.
- Validation: builder.build() must perform validation of required parameters and emit clear exceptions for invalid combos. Validation logic that existed in HTable constructor should be moved here.
- Immutability of built Table: built HTable should copy any mutable data from the builder; HTable's runtime behavior should not depend on a builder instance after construction.
- Deprecation strategy:
  - Keep HTable constructors and mutating setters but mark @Deprecated and Javadoc them as delegating to the builder. Implement them so they set equivalent internal fields to preserve behavior.
  - For public API that previously returned Table directly, implement it by delegating to getTableBuilder(...).build().
  - Document the migration path: prefer TableBuilder APIs; deprecated HTable setters will be removed in a future major release.
- Backward compatibility: ensure no behavioral change surface to callers — default values taken from ConnectionConfiguration must match previous defaults. Add unit/integration tests to assert parity.
- Thread-safety:
  - Builder instances are not required to be thread-safe; document this. If needed, provide a thread-safe factory method on Connection to return immutable preconfigured builders.
  - Built Table/HTable must maintain whatever thread-safety guarantees it had previously.
- Defensive copies: builder setters that accept mutable inputs (byte[] arrays, Maps, Lists) must defensively copy to prevent accidental mutation after build.
- Extension points:
  - TableBuilderBase should be protected-extensible so future specialized builders (e.g., LocalTableBuilder or TestTableBuilder) can reuse common logic.
  - Expose protected hooks for late binding (e.g., override createTableInstance() to return a different Table implementation in tests).
- Error handling: builder.build() should throw checked or unchecked exceptions consistent with previous constructors (prefer existing exception types to minimize API change).

Implementation steps (high level)
1. Create TableBuilderBase with fields for all configuration options and fluent setters. Include validation helpers and defaulting behavior.
2. Create TableBuilder extending TableBuilderBase and implement build() which:
   - Validates
   - Pulls defaults from ConnectionConfiguration (if not already set)
   - Constructs and returns an HTable (or chosen Table implementation) passing final parameters (prefer passing a single immutable config object or the builder itself).
3. Refactor HTable:
   - Add a constructor that accepts a TableBuilder (or the resolved config object).
   - Move configuration/initialization logic into HTable's builder-based constructor.
   - Keep legacy constructors and setters but mark @Deprecated and implement them to modify builder-equivalent fields or delegate to a temporary builder and call initialize logic so behavior is preserved.
4. Modify ConnectionImplementation:
   - Add getTableBuilder(TableName) that constructs a TableBuilder preconfigured with connection-level defaults (including new rpcTimeout getter from ConnectionConfiguration).
   - Make existing getTable(...) implementations delegate to getTableBuilder(...).build().
5. Extend ConnectionConfiguration to expose rpcTimeout (and any other builder-needed fields).
6. Add tests:
   - Unit tests for TableBuilderBase fluent API, defaults, validation.
   - Integration tests asserting that getTable() behavior is identical before and after refactor.
   - Tests for deprecated HTable setters to ensure they still result in the same behavior.
7. Documentation:
   - Update Javadoc on new builder APIs.
   - Add migration notes and mark deprecated methods with planned removal version.

Example API shape (conceptual)
- Connection.getTableBuilder(TableName tableName): TableBuilder
- TableBuilder.rpcTimeout(long ms): TableBuilder
- TableBuilder.someOption(...): TableBuilder
- TableBuilder.build(): Table

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: behavioral regressions if defaults diverge. Mitigation: exhaustive tests comparing built Table behavior before/after refactor; pull defaults from ConnectionConfiguration rather than duplicating them.
- Risk: subtle threading/visibility issues if HTable continues to read mutable builder state after construction. Mitigation: ensure builder-to-HTable handoff copies values and the HTable does not retain references to mutable builder state.
- Risk: deprecation confusion. Mitigation: clearly document migration path; release notes and compile-time @Deprecated warnings.

Acceptance criteria
- All existing public getTable(...) and HTable construction behavior remains unchanged (verified by tests).
- Connection.getTableBuilder(...) returns a preconfigured builder reflecting connection-level defaults (including rpcTimeout).
- HTable’s runtime configuration is derived from builder state; deprecated setters remain supported but emit deprecation warnings.
- New builder API is covered by tests and documented.

Rollout plan
- Implement builder classes and integration tests in feature branch.
- Run full test suite; compare behavioral diffs.
- Merge and release in a minor version with deprecation warnings for HTable setters/constructors.
- Plan removal of deprecated setters in next major release after providing migration guidance.

This directive centralizes construction logic in the Builder, preserves backward compatibility, and makes future configuration extensions and testing easier.

product_owner.prompt:
Title: Centralize table construction/configuration to remove scattered setup and reduce maintenance burden

Description:
Summary
- Construction and configuration logic for tables is currently scattered across multiple places (HTable constructors/setters, ConnectionImplementation, and ConnectionConfiguration). A recent refactor moved that logic into new TableBuilder classes and had getTable delegate to getTableBuilder, but the change mostly relocated existing logic rather than providing a clean, adopted construction API. Deprecated setters were left in HTable for backwards compatibility, and ConnectionConfiguration was extended to expose rpcTimeout for the new builder use. The net result is a partial, inconsistent migration that preserves the old, fragile surface while incrementally adding a second way to build tables.

Pain points / why this is a problem
- Extensibility: Adding new table types or construction options requires touching multiple classes or duplicating code because there is not yet a single, canonical construction API that all callers use.
- Maintainability: Configuration lives in multiple places and is read in different ways (direct setters, constructor args, and builder fields). This leads to duplicated logic and makes it easy to introduce regressions when changing initialization behavior.
- Backwards-compatibility friction: Deprecated setters were left in place as a compatibility shim. That reduces immediate breakage but increases long-term debt because we now have two pathways to configure state (legacy setters + centralized construct), making future removal risky and expensive.
- Inconsistent configuration exposure: Some configuration values required by table construction (eg. rpcTimeout) had to be added to ConnectionConfiguration to support the refactor. We lack a clear, stable surface that exposes all runtime options needed by table construction.
- Testing and debugging difficulty: Because initialization is split, unit/integration tests must mock or cover multiple construction paths. Debugging initialization issues requires tracing through both legacy setters and the new construction flow.
- Slows feature delivery: Feature teams must spend extra time understanding both code paths and may introduce subtle bugs when using legacy setters or partially using the new builder.

Desired outcome / goals
- Make the new centralized construction component the single, authoritative way to build and configure table instances across the codebase.
- Eliminate duplicated initialization code and remove the legacy setters after a scheduled migration window.
- Ensure ConnectionConfiguration exposes a clear, stable set of options required by construction (including rpcTimeout and any future timeouts/settings).
- Update callers (ConnectionImplementation, tests, client code) to consistently use the centralized construction API.
- Improve test coverage around the centralized construction path and add a migration checklist for removing legacy code.

Acceptance criteria
- All internal callers use getTableBuilder (or the canonical construction API) instead of directly constructing/configuring HTable via setters/constructors.
- HTable no longer exposes mutable configuration setters in normal usage; deprecated setters are documented with a removal timeline and flagged for removal once migration completes.
- ConnectionConfiguration documents and exposes all configuration values required by the centralized constructor (including rpcTimeout); no callers depend on private configuration fields.
- Duplication of initialization logic is removed; there is a single code path for building/configuring tables.
- Unit and integration tests are updated to exercise the centralized construction flow; CI passes with these tests.
- A short migration plan and deprecation schedule are added to the repo/RELEASE notes.

Notes / suggested next steps
- Inventory all call sites that construct or configure HTable instances and prioritize migration to the centralized construction API.
- Define and communicate a deprecation timeline for legacy setters (e.g., deprecated now → removal in 2 releases).
- Add examples and documentation showing how to configure tables via the new construction API (including rpcTimeout usage).
- Add tests that assert parity between legacy and centralized initialization behavior before removing legacy code.

tdd.prompt: A senior engineer has written a JUnit test that captures the intended new Builder-style API for Table creation. Refactor the codebase so that the TableBuilder interface and its implementations conform to the new design (fluent setters returning TableBuilder and build() returning Table). Make the test pass without changing the test itself.
